newsitem.title: USA: Glickman post-election comments on Thursday-USDA.
newsitem.headline: Glickman post-election comments on Thursday-USDA.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman will not make post-election comments on farm policy until a speech Thursday, aides said Wednesday.
Glickman was scheduled as luncheon speaker at a conference organized by a Washington consulting firm.

During the campaign, President Clinton pledged to offer legislation next year to strengthen the federal safety net for farmers. A Glickman aide said efforts would focus on how to "tweak," or fine tune, the "Freedom to Farm" law rather than asking for a major revision of it.
Glickman was expected to remain as agriculture secretary.

Aides refused earlier this week to discuss possible turnover among senior policymakers at USDA. Forest Service chief Jack Ward Thomas and Acting Undersecretary for Food Safety Michael Taylor have announced their departures.
According to some analysts, at least four other senior posts could become vacant through resignations.
In the past, Glickman has said he wanted to bolster "risk management" programs for farmers. Those steps could include a more comprehensive crop insurance program and broader use of marketing tools.
